data.title: Cappy first cut: load, shot, ax, query, find, press, doctor
data.description: Cappy is SleepyHollow for native Mac apps; see project/2026-10-19-vision.md (rulings at its end). Mirror sleepy's repo layout, verbs, output formats and exit codes so an agent can switch between them without re-reading help. First user: Penumbra's probe (../Penumbra/scripts/probe), whose in-process captures miss layer-drawn controls, material colors and layer opacity.

data.title: Package skeleton mirroring SleepyHollow
data.description: Package.swift with library Cappy (folders Core, Host, Operations, Output, Session), CappyCLIKit (shared ArgumentParser options), executable cappy, TestSupport and CappyTests, as sleepy has (../sleepyhollow/Package.swift). Swift 6 strict concurrency, macOS 15+. ExitStatus with sleepy's six codes (0 success, 1 negative, 2 usage, 3 timeout, 4 target not found, 5 environment). The bare `cappy` primer and `cappy --help` in sleepy's format; `cappy recipes` (goal-to-verb routing). Target addressing shared by every verb: <app> as bundle ID, name or pid:<n>, plus --window <title|index|id>. A pre-commit hook running swiftformat --lint and swift test, like sleepy's scripts/githooks.

criteria.label: `cappy` with no arguments prints a primer in sleepy's shape, and every verb's --help lists flags, examples and exit codes
Exit codes match sleepy's table, with 4 meaning target not found and 5 a missing permission

data.title: Permission helper app and doctor
data.description: A small signed LSUIElement helper app holds Screen Recording and Accessibility; the CLI talks to it over XPC (vision ruling 1). Its signing identity must be stable across rebuilds so grants persist; document how to build, sign, install and grant it once. `cappy doctor` reports each grant, the helper's path and signature, and the macOS version, and says exactly what to do when something is missing. Never trigger a permission prompt without saying so first; tests needing a grant are tagged and skip with a clear message.

criteria.label: With grants missing, every verb exits 5 with the grant it needs and how to give it
`cappy doctor` reports both grants, the helper and the OS, and exits 5 when anything is missing

data.title: load: is the target there, and its windows
data.description: Mirror `sleepy load`: report the app (name, bundle ID, pid, active), its windows (title, id, frame, key, main, on-screen, minimized) and its appearance (light or dark), as JSON. Exit 4 when no such app or window.

criteria.label: load lists a fixture app's windows with frames that match the app's own report

data.title: ax, query and find: the accessibility tree
data.description: One tree walker over the Accessibility API, with a budget and depth limit that always terminates. `ax` prints sleepy's outline format (one node per line, `role "name" (states)`, indented by depth) or --format json with frames, ids and actions; roles are mapped to readable names the way sleepy's are. `query` matches by role, name, value or identifier and reports frame, enabled, focused, hidden, on-screen and actions. `find` searches titles, values and labels; exit 0 if found, 1 if not. Being an assistive client makes SwiftUI build its tree: test against a fixture app with AppKit and SwiftUI windows, including a SwiftUI checkbox, a pop-up, a disclosure header with an Expanded value, and a control hidden by opacity 0.

criteria.label: ax reads a SwiftUI fixture's heading, checkbox and pop-up with their names and states
A control hidden by opacity 0 or isHidden is reported hidden, not visible

data.title: shot: the composited window
data.description: Mirror `sleepy shot` (--out, --scale, refuse to upsample): capture one window through ScreenCaptureKit, including while it is behind other windows, without raising or activating it; --element <query> crops to an element's frame, --rect to a window rect. Prove what in-process capture misses: a fixture window with a checkbox, a pop-up, secondary text on a sidebar material and a layer at opacity 0 must look as it does on screen.

criteria.label: shot captures a fixture window behind another window without activating it
The checkbox, pop-up bezel and material-colored text appear, and the opacity-0 layer does not

data.title: press: accessibility actions
data.description: Mirror `sleepy click`, named press because it performs an accessibility action: AXPress by default, --action <name> for another (AXShowMenu, AXIncrement), on the element a query names; refuse when the query matches none or several, listing candidates. --point x,y posts a real event at a window point instead. Prove it on SwiftUI controls that synthetic in-process clicks never reach: a Button, a checkbox Toggle, and a tap-gesture disclosure header.

criteria.label: press toggles a SwiftUI fixture checkbox and fires a SwiftUI button, verified by reading ax afterwards

data.title: README, recipes and docs in sleepy's voice
data.description: README like sleepy's: one-line description, what it is, install (experimental-install --product cappy, plus the helper), quick start with load, ax | grep, shot and press, the exit-code table, links. recipes covers every first-cut verb. DocC for the library at 100%.

criteria.label: An agent that knows sleepy can find each first-cut verb from `cappy` and `cappy recipes` alone
